findings.title: Inert data-theme="compat" on <html> — not a canon ThemeId
findings.detail: index.html sets data-theme="compat", but canon ThemeIds are cipher/garden/retro/ocean/sunset/mono/aurora/zen/volt/family/sunlight. tokens.css has no [data-theme="compat"] block, so the html-level attribute is inert. The app re-roots theming at the shell (App.tsx:353 data-theme={theme}), so rendering is correct — the html attr is misleading dead config.
findings.evidence: index.html:2 (data-theme="compat"); canon ThemeId list from useTheme.ts:9 / THEME_IDS; App.tsx:353 overrides at shell level.
findings.recommendation: Remove the html data-theme attribute (or set it to a real canon ThemeId matching the default 'family').

findings.title: Raw hex theme-color in index.html (OS chrome only)
findings.detail: <meta name="theme-color" content="#0a0e14"> is a hardcoded hex. It only affects browser chrome, not the page, but it is not token-driven.
findings.evidence: index.html:8.
findings.recommendation: Set from a token via JS (e.g. resolve --p31-bg at load) or accept as OS-chrome-only.

findings.title: 33 rgba + 5 oklch + 3 hsl CSS literals — documented intentional
findings.detail: Raw color literals exist (glass backgrounds rgba(10,14,20,0.55/0.6), inset highlights rgba(255,255,255,0.5...0.06), shadows rgba(0,0,0,0.25/0.3), amber rgba(255,170,40,...), orb gradients oklch(...), hsl attention-as-light via --loom-light-hue). The porting inventory triage (index.css:1934-1949) documents these as deliberate micro-elements (shadows/highlights/glass) rather than brand surfaces.
findings.evidence: rgba?() count 33 in src/index.css; hsl() at index.css:123,392,567 all token-sourced hue/intensity.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable as-is per project convention; optionally promote the amber/highlight set to tokens for future themes.

findings.title: 10 inline style={{}} sites — all token/layout math, no hardcoded colors
findings.detail: Inline styles feed CSS custom properties (--swatch-color, --artifact-color), set imperative transform positions (AgentCursor), virtualization offsets, and token-var backgrounds (DocsView swatch uses var(--${name})). No hardcoded hex in any inline style.
findings.evidence: slop-eval flags ProposalNode inline_style x1, TraceScale x3; reviewed each site — all layout/token-driven.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable; move AgentCursor/TraceScale transforms to style tokens if desired.

findings.title: 9 non-canon token drift items (--loom-*, --motion-scale, --p31-spring-*)
findings.detail: The app's own port-audit flags --loom-line-height, --loom-light-intensity, --loom-letter-spacing, --loom-panel-width, --loom-light-hue, --motion-scale, and --p31-spring-{fast,default}-spatial/effects as used-but-not-in-canon. These are app-local extension tokens.
findings.evidence: docs/PORTING_INVENTORY.md lists 9 drift items; verified --loom-*/--motion-scale/--p31-spring-* present in src/index.css and absent from canon dist/tokens.css.
findings.recommendation: Either upstream the recurring ones (motion-scale, panel-width) into canon, or document them as app-scoped local tokens.

findings.title: 8 data-agent-actions used in DOM but absent from agent-manifest.json
findings.detail: chain.verify (ChainStatus.tsx), presentation.calm/density/literal/motion/saturation (PresentationControls.tsx), proposal.diff and proposal.why (ProposalCard.tsx) are emitted as data-agent-action but missing from the manifest. 18 manifest actions are never used.
findings.evidence: port-audit regenerated docs/PORTING_INVENTORY.md: 'Used but not in manifest: 8' with the exact list.
findings.recommendation: Add the 8 actions to agent-manifest.json (and prune 18 unused) before next deploy.

findings.title: canon defines [data-spoons] motion scaling but LOOM never sets data-spoons
findings.detail: canon motion.css re-scales durations for data-spoons 0-2 and 4-5, but the Loom app never sets the attribute. LOOM's energy model is attention-as-light (App.tsx:185-193 sets --loom-light-intensity/--loom-light-hue), so spoon-scaling is unused here. The reduced-motion path IS wired (prefers-reduced-motion + --motion-scale + floorMotion), so this is an unused affordance, not a gap.
findings.evidence: rg data-spoons in apps/loom/src and index.html → no matches; canon motion.css defines the selectors.
findings.recommendation: Document the intentional choice, or drop the unused data-spoons styles from canon for this app.

findings.title: Clickable <li> in EventOverlay is not keyboard-operable; no onKeyDown anywhere in the app
findings.detail: Each event row is <li onClick={() => onSelect(e.seq)}> with no role, no tabIndex, and no key handler. Keyboard users cannot open a past event. Grep confirms zero onKeyDown/onKeyUp handlers in the entire app.
findings.evidence: EventOverlay.tsx:31-41; rg onKeyDown src → 0 matches.
findings.recommendation: Add role="button" tabIndex={0} + onKeyDown (Enter/Space) to the li, or wrap each in a real <button>.

findings.title: Reject-reason <input> has no aria-label or <label>
findings.detail: The reason text input is the only editable text field in the app; it has no accessible name. Screen-reader users cannot tell what the field is for.
findings.evidence: ProposalReviewPanel.tsx:65-70 (placeholder='reason (optional)', no label).
findings.recommendation: Add aria-label="Reject reason" or a visible <label>.

findings.title: Timeline scrubber range input has no aria-label
findings.detail: The range slider is unlabeled (the visible 'seq N / M' text is not a label). Contrast: the Jitterbug closure slider has aria-label="Closure".
findings.evidence: TimelineScrubber.tsx:40-47; JitterbugScene.tsx:945 (labeled).
findings.recommendation: Add aria-label="Log position" and aria-valuetext="seq N of M".

findings.title: SoundToggle commits to localStorage only, never the log — inconsistent write path
findings.detail: Every other user action writes to the append-only log via postEvent(fetch /api/loom/event). The sound preference is persisted to localStorage only. It may be intentional (presentation prefs live in localStorage per App.tsx useTheme/usePresentationState), but it breaks the 'every visible state folds over the log' invariant for this control.
findings.evidence: SoundToggle.tsx:17-21 (localStorage loom:sound); App.tsx:74-99 postEvent wiring; README.md 'presentation/theme/sound prefs live in localStorage never the log'.
findings.recommendation: Document as intentional (it already is per README), or post a view.kind event for provenance parity.

findings.title: Canvas surfaces are pointer-only — no keyboard orbit/hit-test equivalent
findings.detail: Instrument click hit-testing (zoom/enter trace) and Jitterbug pointerdown/move orbit, wheel zoom, and raycast focus are mouse/touch-only. Both carry role="img" + aria-label (non-interactive semantics), so AT cannot operate them.
findings.evidence: Instrument.tsx:213-239; JitterbugScene.tsx:670-692, 922.
findings.recommendation: Add arrow-key equivalents for orbit/navigation or document the canvas as a read-only visualization with interactive controls duplicated in DOM.

findings.title: No skip-link or landmark labels
findings.detail: There is no skip-to-content link and no explicit role="main"/aria-label on landmarks. The app is a single-shell SPA, so impact is modest, but keyboard users must tab through the whole top chrome to reach content.
findings.evidence: index.html (no skip link); App.tsx shell has no role=main.
findings.recommendation: Add a skip link and aria-label on the shell region.

findings.title: No <form>/<fieldset>/<label>/<select> semantics app-wide
findings.detail: All interaction is button-driven and writes go via fetch to /api/loom/event; there are no native form semantics anywhere. The reject-reason input is a lone ungrouped text field.
findings.evidence: grep: 0 <form>, 0 <label>, 0 <fieldset>, 0 <select> in apps/loom/src.
findings.recommendation: Group the reject reason + action into a <fieldset> with a <legend>; otherwise acceptable given the app's event-driven model.

findings.title: Lumi.tsx SVG face uses hex fallbacks inside var()
findings.detail: The orb's eyes/mouth use var(--p31-bg, #1a120b) — six hex fallbacks. They are fallbacks only (token is wired), so rendering is token-correct; the hex is a warm-brown intended for the orb face against the token bg.
findings.evidence: Lumi.tsx:49-77.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable; if a future theme changes --p31-bg, the fallback is only pre-theme.

findings.title: scripts/lumi-eval.mjs is broken — imports TS source directly
findings.detail: The CLI imports from '../packages/canon/src/loom/scoring.ts', which internally imports './events.js' (and ./memory.js, ./training.js). Node ESM cannot resolve the .js specifiers to .ts source, so running `node scripts/lumi-eval.mjs` throws ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. The scorer works when imported from the built dist/loom/scoring.js.
findings.evidence: node scripts/lumi-eval.mjs → ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND .../canon/src/loom/events.js (exit from the tool). Running the equivalent against dist/loom/scoring.js passes: good meets all floors, bad/hard-bad fail as designed.
findings.recommendation: Change lumi-eval.mjs to import from '../packages/canon/dist/loom/scoring.js' (or add a TS loader).

findings.title: LUMI eval scorer + canon substrate verified healthy (positive finding)
findings.detail: Scoring is deterministic (five phases with FLOORS planning .5 / safety 1 / coPresence .5 / memory .4 / structure .5), bad samples are designed to fail and do, memory is a consent-gated four-tier fold, training is shared-scope-only, and the writer-per-kind gate is enforced. All canon loom tests pass.
findings.evidence: lumi-eval via dist: good {planning:1,safety:1,coPresence:1,memory:1,structure:1}; bad {safety:0,coPresence:0}; hard-bad {safety:0,coPresence:0}. canon test-loom-{gate,review,memory,training,drift,determinism} all green.
findings.recommendation: None — maintain.

findings.title: Auto-propose timer is timing-based agent behavior
findings.detail: Lumi auto-proposes 3.5s after the child taps the orb, and CreativeChapter formalizes each color pick as an agent propose. These are deterministic arcs; no model identity is used (per Lumi.tsx docstring) and all writes pass the gate. No concern beyond noting agent behavior is time-triggered.
findings.evidence: App.tsx:154-174; CreativeChapter.tsx:65-81.
findings.recommendation: None — note only.

findings.title: APCA validator is design-core-specific — canon tokens are not actually contrast-validated
findings.detail: Running validate-apca.mjs against canon dist/tokens.css yields 0 fails but 19/19 checks skipped: the MATRIX pairs reference design-core token names (--p31-text on --p31-bg/surface-s*) and canon uses a different token vocabulary (--p31-text-primary, --p31-layout-* etc.). There is no canon-specific contrast gate.
findings.evidence: node .../validate-apca.mjs canon/dist/tokens.css --json → 19 checks, 19 skipped, 0 fails. MATRIX in validate-apca.mjs is design-core pairs.
findings.recommendation: Add a canon-token APCA matrix (or parametrize the validator) so the family/theme palettes get contrast coverage.

findings.title: LOOM src scores 12 on the generic slop-eval — inflated by hex fallbacks, not raw slop
findings.detail: The chat portal's slop-eval counts every #hex occurrence regardless of whether it's a var() fallback. index.css has 196 hex (all var(--p31-*, #fallback)) + 104 rgba (shadows/highlights) + 1 emoji (U+2733 dingbat used as a node label prefix in App.tsx:288) + 1 rgba in JitterbugScene (comment) + inline styles in TraceScale/ProposalNode (layout math). Raw score 12 = 'definitely-slop', but this is a counting artifact, not slop.
findings.evidence: node .../portals/chat/scripts/slop-eval.mjs --dir src --json → score 12; detail list shows the 196-hex/104-rgba fallback inflation; verified each flagged file.
findings.recommendation: Do not rely on the chat slop-eval for LOOM. Add a canon-aware slop evaluator that ignores var() fallbacks, or extend the raw-value triage in port-audit.

findings.title: apps/loom/ is not tracked in git — no CI/regression baseline
findings.detail: git status shows `?? apps/loom/` — the entire directory is untracked in the production repo. This audit's findings and the regenerated docs/PORTING_INVENTORY.md cannot be diffed, and no deploy/CI gate references them.
findings.evidence: git -C /home/p31/production status --short apps/loom/ → '?? apps/loom/'.
findings.recommendation: Decide the repo boundary for apps/loom (track it here or in its own repo as .gitignore hints) so audit artifacts version.
